findings.summary: The overload-shed load tests (resolve read-load `1a5d`, create-load `2b6e`) assert 'beyond a safe-overload margin the path fast-fails and sheds', but the 'safe-overload margin' is named only qualitatively in both SPEC §6 and TDD §4 — no concrete multiplier or absolute rate is defined. The read design-load anchors to ~10^6 links and @threshold:PRD.01.rate.redirectsustained, but the shed trip point (the margin above design load at which fast-fail must engage) has no number a test can target. A test asserting 'sheds beyond the margin' with no defined margin is a tautology: any shed point passes, including one that sheds at design load (false-negative on capacity regression) or one that never sheds before pool exhaustion.
findings.recommendation: Quantify the safe-overload margin in SPEC §6 as a concrete factor of design load (e.g., shed engages at >= K x sustained rate) and have `1a5d`/`2b6e` assert the bounded degraded/shed response at exactly that K, plus a paired assertion that p95 still holds AT design load (margin lower edge). Without the literal number these two type:performance cases cannot satisfy C2.

findings.summary: Standby-loss durability halt (ADR.01.05.5896): `81b4` asserts DurabilityHaltError fail-closed (failure detected) and states 'the retry is retryable on standby recovery using bounded backoff' — but this is a property claim about retryability, not an executed recovery assertion. The test does not appear to restore the standby and assert put_mapping subsequently succeeds idempotently. Per C1 a chaos scenario needs both (a) failure detected AND (b) recovery when the failure clears actually exercised; here recovery is asserted by description, not by a restore-then-succeed step, so the impl could stay permanently halted (never re-admitting writes after standby returns) undetected.
findings.recommendation: Extend `81b4` (or add a paired e2e) to: inject standby loss -> assert DurabilityHaltError -> restore standby -> assert the retried identical put_mapping succeeds and the durability-halt signal clears. Mirror the degrade->recover pattern already present in `4d80`.

findings.summary: SPEC §6 explicitly calls out 'bounded exponential backoff with jitter so a synchronized retry does not storm the recovering standby'. `81b4` asserts 'bounded backoff with jitter (no storm)' as a property of a single retry, but does not exercise the actual cascade: many DurabilityHalt'd writers retrying concurrently the moment the standby recovers. The retry-storm path (legitimate clients all backing off and re-firing in sync) is the named reliability risk and is the one condition the jitter exists to defend — yet it is asserted, not load-driven. An impl with backoff-without-jitter (or insufficient jitter) would pass `81b4` as written while still storming the recovering standby in production.
findings.recommendation: Add an integration case that halts N concurrent writers on standby loss, restores the standby, and asserts the retry arrival distribution is spread (no synchronized thundering herd) and the standby is not re-saturated on recovery — turning the jitter claim into an exercised assertion.
